key_insight: DeepFEAv2 extends deep-learning surrogate modeling to transient finite element analysis on both structured and unstructured meshes while jointly predicting node- and element-based outputs over time.
engineering_relevance: This enables much faster transient mechanical simulation workflows for real-time analysis, high-resolution studies, and broader mesh-compatible deployment in engineering design.
method: Uses the FE connectivity matrix to organize element-wise input features into a mesh-topology-guided sequence.
Introduces a neural architecture that processes this sequence to jointly predict node- and element-based outputs over time.
Adds an FEA-informed regularization strategy to improve physical consistency of predictions.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on structured and unstructured 3D linear elastic datasets and a pressure-driven aortic valve case, achieving R² up to 0.99, normalized error as low as 0.38%, and inference up to three orders of magnitude faster than traditional FEA.
watch_item: Performance may depend on accurate mesh connectivity and careful adaptation to new element types or highly complex geometries.
paper_title: DeepFEAv2: Deep Learning for Transient Finite Element Analysis Beyond Structured Meshes
